texts: A symptomatic 90% carotid stenosis together with critical left main and right coronary disease is best treated by synchronous carotid endarterectomy and CABG.
His recent right-hemisphere attacks make a stroke during bypass a real danger, while his left main disease makes a carotid operation alone dangerous for the heart.
Doing both under one anaesthetic protects the brain and the heart together.
Staging them a week apart leaves him exposed to the untreated lesion: a stroke during CABG, or an infarction during endarterectomy.
Carotid stenting first needs dual antiplatelet therapy, which delays CABG and adds bleeding.
In the picture, Zoro scrapes the carrot while Sanji lays the cabbage, as the two clocks strike together.
Memory hook: a flickering lantern and a squeezed main: carrot and cabbage at the same stroke.
